sections.html:
A direct cash sale can close on your calendar, often within a few weeks, because no lender has to approve the buyer. You trade some price for speed and certainty, so set any offer beside a listing estimate before you decide.

Population is 122,492 and rising quickly, up 35.5 percent from the 2020 base. Growth means plenty of new listings, and a tired house competes with newer builds.

Owners usually choose a quick sale for reasons like these:

  • Relocating along the I-35 corridor toward Austin or San Antonio.
  • An older home needing repairs that financed buyers will not accept.
  • A short-term or vacation rental that no longer pays off.
  • An inherited house shared among several heirs.
  • A code, title or tax problem on the property.

sections.h2: Which county is your house in?
sections.html:
New Braunfels is the seat of Comal County, but the city also reaches into Guadalupe County. Some parcels therefore sit under a different county than the name suggests. Your tax bill shows which appraisal district covers your lot, and that same county's clerk will record your deed.

The city is in the San Antonio metro area, so many sellers deal with buyers relocating from there or commuting along Interstate 35 and Farm Road 725. Older neighborhoods near Landa Park and the river have a long German-era history, while newer subdivisions sit on the edge of town. Tell any buyer which kind of street you are on, and mention any flood or drainage history, since the rivers shape much of the area.

sections.h2: Home values and the local market
sections.html:
Values here run well above those in smaller Texas towns. A stable, owner-heavy base gives buyers plenty of choices, and a visibly worn house is easy to skip.

Commuters who buy often want a move-in-ready house near I-35 or Farm Road 725. A home that needs updates may do better with an investor than with a typical family buyer.

sections.h2: Appraisal district and property tax rules
sections.html:
For Comal County parcels, the Comal Appraisal District values the property and handles exemptions. The office is at 900 S. Seguin Ave., New Braunfels, and is open weekdays. April 15 and May 15 are dates to watch. If your parcel lies in Guadalupe County, ask the tax office there who appraises it.

Homeowners get a school district exemption of $140,000, and a homestead's appraised value cannot rise more than 10 percent a year once the exemption has been in place. The cap starts the January 1 after the exemption first applies. School taxes can be frozen for senior and disabled owners.

  • Value date: January 1.
  • Protest deadline: mid-May in most cases.
  • Delinquency: February 1 after a January 31 deadline.

The cap helps long-term owners but resets for a buyer, so a recent sale can raise the bill for the next owner. Bring that up when you talk price.

sections.h2: Selling a rented or short-term rental house
sections.html:
River and lake visitors have made short stays common here, so plenty of houses have been rentals. If yours is rented now, the tenant's rights set the timeline. A landlord who wants the tenant out normally serves a written notice to vacate, three days unless the lease sets something else, and only after that can ask a justice court to step in.

Call the City of New Braunfels about any permit or registration tied to a short-term rental before you transfer the property, since requirements can differ by address. An investor will want the rental history and any open compliance issue up front.

Move quickly if payments have slipped. Once a default notice arrives you have 20 days to bring the loan current. Foreclosure auctions happen on the first Tuesday of the month at a spot the commissioners court designates, and the sale posting must go up at least three weeks beforehand.

Tax liens run on their own track. One attaches each January 1, and after February 1 penalties and interest build, with an added collection penalty of up to 20 percent if the taxing unit hires a private attorney. Both payoffs come out of your proceeds at closing, so ask the title company for exact numbers.

The right path depends on condition and timing. A cash offer suits a place that needs repairs or an owner with a firm deadline. A listing may net more for a polished house in a strong subdivision.

  • Cash offer: no repairs, you pick the date, no financing contingency.
  • Traditional listing: higher potential price, plus commissions, repairs and showings.
  • Sale to an heir or relative: may need a deed and clear title paperwork.

Ask each buyer for a written offer and compare the net you would keep after payoffs and fees.

sections.h2: How a quick sale unfolds, step by step
sections.html:
Start by collecting your latest tax bill, your mortgage statement and any lease. Request written offers from more than one buyer, then line them up against a realistic listing estimate for the same house.

Once you accept an offer, the title company opens the file, checks for liens and unpaid taxes, and schedules the signing. If the title is clean, nothing much stands between you and the closing date you chose. If a lien, a missing heir or a tenant turns up, ask the buyer to put the new timeline in writing.

Do not pay anyone upfront to receive an offer. A fair buyer covers the normal closing costs listed in the contract, and you should see every line before signing.

The title company prepares the deed and settlement statement, and the county clerk where the property sits files the deed. The signature must be notarized or otherwise officially acknowledged before the deed can be recorded.

Recording starts at five dollars for the first page. Call the Comal County Clerk, or the Guadalupe County Clerk if your parcel is there, for the current schedule.

Before closing day, gather your photo ID, mortgage payoff details if you owe anything, and keys and garage openers. The title company confirms the payoffs, subtracts them and any tax owed, and hands you the balance. A cash sale skips the lender appraisal and the loan underwriting, which is where many traditional deals slip.

faqs.q: How fast can a New Braunfels sale close?
faqs.a: Often in a few weeks if the title is clear. A shared inheritance, a lien or a tenant adds time. Ask for the closing date in writing with the offer.

faqs.q: Is New Braunfels in Comal or Guadalupe County?
faqs.a: Both. The city is the Comal County seat and extends into Guadalupe County. Your tax bill shows which county's appraisal district applies.

faqs.q: What does a typical New Braunfels house cost?
faqs.a: The median for owner-held homes is $339,400. Your own price depends on condition, location and size, so treat that figure as context only.

faqs.q: Can I sell a New Braunfels house with foundation or roof problems?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers take on the repairs themselves, and the offer accounts for them. Compare it with a repaired listing estimate to see which nets more.

faqs.q: When are New Braunfels property tax protests due?
faqs.a: Mid-May in most cases. The Comal Appraisal District highlights April 15 and May 15, so call the office to confirm your date.
